main_text.p: nim ipsis insita suavitas est, ut magis voluptatis gratia eos confectos quis diceret. Licet igitur usque ad tria cochlearia indies ex eis sumere, maximè si cibus prius in utentre sit probè concoctus. Qui enim eos accipiunt, melius concoquunt, & cibos appetunt: floridius etiam corpus habent, & sensus, omnes vegetiores. Haec Aetius de Salium theriacorum praestantia adversus omnis elephantiae profligationem: quorum loco serpentibus, qui saxosis in locis degunt, pauperibus uti licebit, si viperarum instar parentur. Postremò ob raucedinem, quae elephanticos omnes semper comitatur, lac quotidie sumere operaepretium fuerit. Expurgetur item cerebrum, apophle-gmatismis, errhinis, & sternutatoriis, capitisque ustio fiat, quemadmodum Cap.1.2. iubet Aegineta libro quarto, & sexto de Re medica.

page.notes: The margin note "Cap.1.2." is faint. Right-hand faded text below the main text is show-through from the reverse page and was left out. Long s, u/v and i/j normalised as per the rules; Greek and other words not present. "Licet" written whole because the line break "Li-cet" has no printed hyphen. Some faint letters in the lower-left show-through were not transcribed.
